title: Unlabeled zone (edge): a party whose signature says London writes "Thursday at 2pm" with no zone; Thursday 9:00am ET (2pm in London) and 2:00pm ET were both offered. State the assumption or ask.
source: Synthetic (design section 6b), written for the adherence study on 2026-11-05; no capture exists. Calendar generated by scenarios/synthetic/calendar.ts from Bob's weekly pattern (titles, attendees and places in the captured fixtures' anonymized vocabulary), the scheduling policy is plan 39's (Winnie's config at ca6b6ee). In November London is UTC+0 and Bob is UTC-5: 2pm London is 9am Eastern.

review.answer: Bob, 2026-11-05: ask her; do not guess.
review.question: Tatum (London signature) writes "Thursday at 2pm"; 9am ET (2pm London) and 2pm ET were both offered, in ET. The expectation is to ask her which. Would you rather she book 2pm ET as written (the offers were in ET) and tell you the assumption, or book 9am ET reading her zone from the signature?

thread.text:
Hi,

+Winnie (agent) to help us schedule this one. Could you find us 30 minutes this week for a
partnership call? Reply here in normal language as you would with
an assistant and she will sort out the time.

Bob

Hello,

I'm Winnie, Bob's virtual assistant. Bob asked me to set up 30 minutes with you on a Meet link. Here are times that work on his side:

- Thu, Nov 19, 9:00am to 9:30am ET
- Thu, Nov 19, 2:00pm to 2:30pm ET
- Fri, Nov 20, 11:00am to 11:30am ET

If one of those suits, say so and I will send the invite. If none do, send me a couple of times that work for you and I will check them.

Winnie
Virtual scheduling assistant to Bob, Example Co

sent.summary: Offered three times on a Meet link, Bob in cc.

events.trigger: Tatum Rhee replied on the thread.

thread.text:
Thursday at 2pm works for me.

Best,
Tatum Rhee
Partner, Northgate Advisory
14 Fenchurch Avenue, London

expect.basis: What a careful assistant does: two offered slots fit "Thursday at 2pm" once the zone is open (562 as written in ET, 561 in London time), so she asks which, the loop's own "if two offered slots fit their words, ask them which" applied to zones.
expect.notes: EDGE: Winnie has no rule for a zone read from a signature; the accept rule matches clocks, and the mail she sent was in ET, so a literal match books 562 without a question. FOR BOB (the review question).
